shortlist.label: Pituitary adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm, abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone level, and elevated prolactin level

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual reduction, sellar/suprasellar mass, and endocrine dysfunction

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass, bitemporal hemianopsia, and history of vestibular schwannoma

shortlist.label: Pituitary apoplexy
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual reduction, sellar/suprasellar mass, and history of pituitary disease

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass, abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone level, and elevated prolactin level, with potential for systemic disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with rapidly progressive visual reduction, bitemporal hemianopsia, and a sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm, along with abnormal endocrinological findings such as elevated prolactin, is most consistent with a pituitary adenoma.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Typically presents in childhood or adolescence and often has calcifications on imaging, which were not mentioned.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Usually has a dural tail sign on imaging and is less likely to cause significant endocrinological abnormalities.

rejected.label: Pituitary apoplexy
rejected.why: Typically presents with sudden onset of severe headache, visual loss, and altered mental status, which does not match the patient's gradual progression of symptoms.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Less likely to cause a well-defined sellar/suprasellar mass and would typically have more systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy.
